passage:
In economics class, students traced the life of a cotton T-shirt. The cotton was grown in one country, made into cloth in another, sewn in a third, and sold in a fourth.
The students were surprised. A simple shirt had traveled farther than many people.
They discussed water use, factory work, shipping, price, and waste. Some students said cheap clothes were helpful for families with less money. Others worried that low prices could hide environmental or labor costs.
The teacher said the goal was not to make shopping impossible. It was to make it less blind.
A T-shirt is not only clothing. It is a map of global choices.
